evidence: verify-bundle.sh only drove the top-level reviewThreads truncation; 06e18a4 adds write_pr_fixture's thread-truncated flaw and refuses_capture cases for the errors document, pullRequest:null and a shapeless document, each asserting nonzero exit, named refusal and no index.json.
guidance_note: When a module's stated purpose is refusing bad input, write one fixture per refusal branch in the original PR rather than only the headline case.

evidence: parse_step's sys.exit and elapsed's None return had no exercising input; 06e18a4 section 7 pipes a tab-less row and an unparseable clock through bundle.py and asserts the exit text and duration_seconds None.
guidance_note: Same as F1: every loud-failure branch a new module adds ships with a test that drives it.

evidence: The script used chmod, diff and cat without horizon_need while sibling verifiers declare them; 06e18a4 adds the three declarations. It did not sweep the rest of the file's external commands, which is why F22, F28 and F34 followed.
guidance_note: When adding a tool-declaration block, grep the whole script for every external command it runs and declare all of them in one pass, not just the ones the reviewer named.

evidence: The exact-equality cwd test made a claude -p run from a worktree under the project FOREIGN and dropped its spend; the agent confirmed it bit in practice and 06e18a4 adds within() containment plus a worktree-subprocess test and foreign_transcripts count.
guidance_note: When widening a predicate, list every consumer of its result (here SESSION eligibility and the all-foreign abort) and test each boundary the docstring names, which would have pre-empted F11 and F20.

evidence: Dedup kept the first block's usage on an unchecked assumption; 06e18a4 made billed a dict and sys.exit on disagreement. That exit was later found (local medium, 9c21dec) to kill a live poll and was changed to a count, and the docstring that still said 'stops' became F32.
guidance_note: Before turning an assumption into a sys.exit, check every caller of the code path; sessions.py runs on the 2-second live poll where any nonzero exit kills the run.

evidence: The PR put a fallible date read with horizon_die between horizon_take_run_lock and the EXIT trap, so a failure would strand the tmux lock; 06e18a4 moves the read above the lock.
guidance_note: When a file documents a window that must hold nothing fallible, check every line you add or move into that window against it.

evidence: thread['comments']['pageInfo']['hasNextPage'] bypassed connection() and would raise a bare KeyError; 06e18a4 generalises the walker to captured(root, path, subject) and routes every structural read, including FLAT_FIELDS, through it, with a shapeless-document gate check.
guidance_note: When a module promises one loud-on-drift reader, grep for bare subscripts on the captured document before shipping.

evidence: A missing transcripts/ made sessions.py glob nothing and write an all-zero loop.json; 06e18a4 makes horizon_capture_loop refuse when the directory is absent while keeping an empty directory legal, which was the reviewer's second option.
guidance_note: For each capture that reads a predecessor's output, decide in the original PR what 'predecessor did not land' looks like and refuse on it.

evidence: The same project-dir guard and message appeared verbatim in three capture functions; 06e18a4 extracts horizon_require_bundle_project and calls it from all three.
guidance_note: When pasting a guard into a third function, extract it instead.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the abort `if foreign and not sessions` is in the original PR diff (hunk shows it as an addition before review), and 06e18a4 did not touch it, so a SUBPROCESS plus a FOREIGN transcript triggered the false 'all another project's' message before the fix too. 1b65b2c adds `and not subprocesses` with two tests.
guidance_note: When an abort's message makes a universal claim ('all another project's'), write the predicate as the negation of every bucket that could falsify it, and test with one transcript of each kind.

evidence: within() from 06e18a4 widened SESSION eligibility too, and only the subprocess case was documented and tested. The risk the reviewer named is unreachable because the config dir is wiped per run under the lock, and an agent moving into a worktree is legitimate. So the agent declined the gating and took the reviewer's alternative: an interactive-worktree test plus a comment.
guidance_note: When the F4 fix widened `belongs`, it should have documented and tested the effect on every classification that reads it, not just the one that motivated the change.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: `|| return 0` in horizon_bundle_project_dir is pre-review code that 06e18a4 did not touch, and 06e18a4 only moved the misleading message into the extracted helper. The agent logged the unreadable-manifest case instead of making it fatal, because a die in the exit-handler close-out would lose run.json, and reworded the refusal. That reworded refusal later became F35.
guidance_note: A refusal message should name only what the check observed, not the cause it assumes.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the died-scenario's reuse of $CONFIG is pre-review test code that 06e18a4 did not change. It only worked because section 1 had moved $CONFIG/projects away. 1b65b2c gives it its own config dir with no projects/, and the agent noticed that an empty projects/ would test the opposite case.
guidance_note: Each test scenario should build its own inputs rather than inheriting state an earlier section left behind.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the inline $(json_field ...) passed as one argument to sessions.py is in the pre-review hunk. bash ignores the failure status of a substitution used as an argument, so the json_field refusal was lost. 1b65b2c assigns it to RECORDED_PROJECT first, and the agent mutation-tested the change.
guidance_note: In set -e scripts, never pass a command substitution that can fail as an argument to another command; assign it to a variable first.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: the all-foreign abort and the cwd-less-equals-FOREIGN classification were in the original PR. The agent's issue comment confirms a real unattended run died at minute zero, and e70e51f (local escalation review) had already added the FORMING state before this thread was read.
guidance_note: Before adding an exit to code, list every process that calls it; this abort was correct at close-out but fatal on the live 2-second poll.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: elapsed() is unchanged pre-review code; 06e18a4 only added tests for its unparseable branch. A finish before start returned a negative int, against the docstring's own principle, and 1b65b2c returns None with a mutation-tested gate check.
guidance_note: When a function's docstring states a principle (a non-number for an untrustworthy record), list every input class that violates it, including reversed order, not just unparseable input.

evidence: No code path writes *.partial (staging is mktemp under TMPDIR), so the find assertion could never fail. The dead check came from the agent's own 9c21dec fix for a local medium-review finding, which has no thread in this packet, so no finding id can be named. The agent took the reviewer's second option and asserted exact bundle contents.
guidance_note: After changing a design (staging inside the bundle moved to staging outside), re-run every assertion written for the old design, and mutation-test it to confirm it can still fail.

evidence: within() re-ran realpath(root) for every cwd-bearing line on every 2-second poll. That root-side realpath came from the agent's local e70e51f fix ('within() realpaths both sides'), not a thread finding. Hoisting would have made within() unsafe for an unnormalised root, so memoising per distinct cwd is sound.
guidance_note: When making a helper normalise its loop-invariant argument, cache the result at the call site in the same change.

evidence: The run.json literals in verify-bundle.sh are independent expectations about the public bundle contract and fixture inputs. Deriving them from HORIZON_BUNDLE_RECORD would make the gate follow a rename silently. The agent also found and reasoned about the real duplicate spelling inside HORIZON_BUNDLE_LAYOUT.

06e18a4's within() docstring names the /a/project-two collision as the reason for `+ os.sep`, but the F4 fix's tests covered only the worktree case. 8a929ad adds a sibling-directory test, and the agent mutation-killed dropping the separator.
guidance_note: Every edge case a docstring names as a design reason gets a test in the same commit that adds the docstring.

evidence: The bundle README paragraph said 'total is the sum' and then 'the four figures are kept apart rather than added into one number', which contradicts itself, and 'four' had no referent. The 06e18a4 diff does not touch this paragraph, and the packet does not show which commit introduced it, so no cause is assigned.
guidance_note: Prose that summarises two different axes (session/subprocess/total vs four token types) should give each axis its own sentence, mirroring the developer README that already did.

evidence: 06e18a4 added horizon_need for diff/cat/chmod (F3), and the same commit's section 6 introduced `cut` without declaring it; `head` came later. The agent also caught that its own first *.partial replacement used undeclared `ls`.
guidance_note: When fixing an undeclared-tool finding, grep the whole script (and your own new code in the same commit) for every external command rather than adding only the named ones.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: bundle.py's direct open(...,'w') for run.json is pre-review code that 1b65b2c only touched in elapsed(). The local 9c21dec staging sweep missed it while every other bundle write stages and moves. 8a929ad uses NamedTemporaryFile plus os.replace.
guidance_note: When adopting stage-and-move for one bundle write, list every writer into the bundle (shell and Python) and convert them all in the same commit.

evidence: The README promised run.json for a run that 'died holding the lock', but the close-out's `[ ! -d bundle_dir ]` early return, added by the agent's local 9c21dec fix, writes nothing. This is doc drift from a fix with no thread in the packet. 8a929ad qualifies the guarantee.
guidance_note: When a fix adds an early return that skips the record, grep the docs for the guarantee it now carves an exception from.

evidence: time-zero.json was the last bundle file written by direct redirect after F23 and 866c472 staged run.json, index.json and the README. The reviewer concedes a truncated file would fail loudly at the watermark parse, so this is a consistency gap, not a silent failure. 71f3de2 stages it, with a gate check.
guidance_note: Same as F23: the staging sweep should have enumerated writers by grepping for `>` into $bundle_dir, including ones that run before the close-out.

evidence: The TMPDIR leak is real, but the proposed `|| { rm -f; }` is unreachable because horizon_report and horizon_lit_export end in horizon_die, which exits. A trap risks clobbering run-loop.sh's single lock-releasing EXIT trap. The staging came from the agent's local e70e51f/9c21dec fixes, not a thread finding.

866c472, the F17 fix, wrote case arms `'"'"'*'"'"'` that decode to a 5-character pattern and never match. The agent says it mechanically applied an escaping idiom to a quoted heredoc. 71f3de2 replaces the glob loop with find, removing the arms.
guidance_note: When generating shell through a heredoc, run the emitted line in a scratch shell before committing instead of reasoning about quoting.

evidence: This was the third extension of the same horizon_need list: `basename` came in with the 866c472 F17 fix and `dirname` from an earlier fixture. 71f3de2 declares dirname and removes basename's only use.
guidance_note: After two findings on the same declaration list, sweep the script mechanically (e.g. list every command word) instead of adding the reviewer's names.

evidence: Review fixes added subprocess_transcripts (1b65b2c, F10), plus forming_transcripts, usage_disagreements and tokens.unattributed (local e70e51f/9c21dec). The developer README mentioned none of them, though two of them halt the close-out. 71f3de2 adds two paragraphs.
guidance_note: Every fix that adds an output key or a refusal updates the developer README section describing that output in the same commit.

evidence: Full state=all pagination does grow with the campaign, but at per_page=100 a thousand PRs is ten calls once per run. A hand-rolled early-stop risks silently dropping this run's PRs, which is the failure the bundle exists to prevent. The flag is a false positive: the gh api --paginate call is unchanged pre-review code.

assistant_block always sets an id, so message_key's ('entry', line) fallback is untested. The agent agreed on merit and even described the exact test, yet deferred 'for scope' with no ticket filed, leaving a known, few-line gap on a merged PR. The flag is a false positive: the fallback is pre-review code.
guidance_note: A cheap test whose content the agent can already state is written, not deferred; when deferring, file the ticket rather than offering to.

evidence: 06e18a4 (F5 fix) rewrote message_key's docstring to say read_transcript 'stops if it ever stops being true'. The later local 9c21dec change replaced the exit with a count and left that docstring stale, which the agent admits. cf0c4e7 corrects it and points to the handling site.
guidance_note: When reversing a behaviour (exit to count), grep for every prose description of the old behaviour, including docstrings in other functions.

evidence: `usage.get(field) or 0` would read a renamed key as zero, but the trigger is a hypothetical schema change, and the reviewer's 'fail loud' would kill the live poll. The agent's alternative (a counted field plus a close-out refusal) is a larger change. No ticket was filed. The flag is a false positive: usage_of is pre-review code.
guidance_note: When deferring a real but speculative gap, file the tracking ticket in the same reply instead of offering to.

evidence: `date` is used in run-loop.sh (the start read that F6 moved) and in the close-out but was never declared via horizon_need. This is the same undeclared-tool class as F3/F22/F28, in a script those sweeps never covered. cf0c4e7 declares it.
guidance_note: When a tool-declaration finding recurs, sweep every script in the directory, not only the one the reviewer pointed at.

evidence: 1b65b2c (F12 fix) rewrote the refusal to say 'seed/ is in the bundle, look there', which is false for the died-before-seeding bundle that verify-bundle.sh section 2 builds. The old message was right for that case. cf0c4e7 rewords it to name whether seed/ exists as the discriminator.
guidance_note: When rewording a message to cover two causes, check it against each existing test scenario that reaches it, including the one with no seed/ at all.

evidence: e70e51f (the F15 fix) added FORMING as a separate state but left the abort's '%d found, all another project's' counting only foreign, so forming transcripts were silently omitted from a universal claim. cf0c4e7 names them separately and adds a coexistence test.
guidance_note: When adding a new enum state, grep every place the old states are counted or described in messages and decide the new state's place in each.

narrative: This is a large horizon bundle-capture PR with 36 CI findings over 9 rounds (4 cancelled by later pushes), interleaved with local high/medium/escalation reviews whose fixes have no threads here. Most findings were real, and the agent's judgment was strong: it pushed back correctly on F19, F26 and F30, chose better fixes on F12, F18 and F27, and mutation-tested nearly every fix. About a third of later-round findings were caused by earlier fixes: an undeclared-tool list extended four times, docs and docstrings drifting from the exit-to-count and FORMING changes, a reworded message that broke the case it was meant to cover, and a quoting bug in a test-check rewrite. Every round with findings also had fresh pre-existing findings, so no round was wholly avoidable.
guidance_observations: The same undeclared-tool finding recurred four times (F3, F22, F28, F34) because each fix added only the names the reviewer listed; one mechanical sweep of every script's command words would have closed the class.

Behaviour reversals made during review (exit to count, three to four transcript states) were not followed by a grep for prose and messages describing the old behaviour, which produced F29, F32 and F36.
Two deferrals (F31, F33) ended with 'happy to file a ticket' rather than a filed ticket, leaving known gaps untracked at merge.
Local review fixes (9c21dec, e70e51f) introduced several defects CI later found (F17, F18, F24, F26), so fix-caused cost is undercounted by the thread-level chains.
